p1: The Lord had just chosen Jeremiah to share His words. Then the Lord asked him, “Jeremiah, what do you see?”
Jeremiah looked closely. He said, “I see a branch from an almond tree.” In spring, the almond tree wakes up first, with early blossoms.
The Lord said, “You have seen well.” Jeremiah had looked carefully and seen it right.
p2: Then the Lord said, “I will hurry to make My word come true.” Like the early almond, His word would never be late. The Lord was Jesus, and what He says really happens. Jeremiah could feel sure, even when people would not listen.
The Lord keeps His promises to you too. You can trust Him, every single day.
old: One day Heavenly Father asked Jeremiah a question. "Jeremiah, what do you see?" Jeremiah looked, and then he looked again. "I see a little branch from an almond tree," he said. A branch is one small arm of a tree.

The almond tree is the very first tree to wake up in spring. The other trees are still brown and sleepy, but the almond tree opens little white flowers like tiny stars. In Jeremiah's language, the name of the almond tree sounds almost like the word for watching. So the waking branch meant: Someone is awake and watching!

"You have seen well," Heavenly Father said. "I am watching over My promises, to make them come true." Heavenly Father was saying, "I am wide awake, like that almond tree, and I will keep every promise I make."

You can be a good looker like Jeremiah. Tomorrow, look closely at a tree, a flower, or the morning sun. Every good thing you see can remind you: Heavenly Father is awake, keeping His promises, and watching over you.
